newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says many in Zaire still need help.
newsitem.headline: Canada says many in Zaire still need help.

text.p: Hundreds of thousands of refugees in Zaire still need assistance despite the exodus of displaced Rwandans who have crossed the border and returned home, a Canadian official said on Tuesday.

"We can't be misled here by thinking that the 500,000 people that have crossed the border -- and that's a very impressive number -- represents the totality of the people," International Cooperation Minister Don Boudria said in an interview with the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation.

Canada is leading the planned humanitarian rescue mission for Rwanda refugees but the military scope of the mission is under review. The United States said on Tuesday it was scaling back the number of military personnel it was sending, and Canada and its allies are examining how its mission should be amended in light of the mass exodus of refugees from the Goma area of Zaire east into Rwanda over the past week.
"First of all, you have to imagine that those who crossed the border were obviously the ones who were closest to it," Boudria said.

"The ones that went inland, for instance towards the further western positions inside Zaire, those people have not yet reached the border. We don't know whether they can, we don't know whether they're still at the mercy of local warlords, warring factions, different military groups and so on," he said.

"Secondly, there's a whole group of people, several hundreds of thousands of them, that are on the south side of Lake Kivu (around Bukavu), and those people, as far as we know, have not moved in large numbers.

"And finally, there's a third group, further south, opposite Burundi (around Uvira), and then there's a whole group of inland refugees of Zaire -- in other words, the people who are displaced within their own country. Those are not people who are Rwandans or Burundians. They're Zairians -- almost refugees inside their own country."

Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and Defense Minister Doug Young on Monday raised the possibility that troops might no longer be needed if conditions continued to improve. But Chretien said he believed troops were still needed and Young said it was too early to say the crisis was over since hundreds of thousands of refugees remained in Zaire.
While assessments were being made, Canada was holding back the deployment of the bulk of its force. It has sent about 200 reconnaissance personnel but they have not been able to do much scouting.
